rationale: One clause -- "leather belt around his waist" -- is identical, word for word, in this app's own BSB rendering of both verses, checkable directly without a secondary source. The rest of the description is a looser match: Matthew states John wore "a garment of camel's hair," a piece of clothing, while 2 Kings 1:8 states Elijah "was a hairy man," which the NET Bible's own translator's note reads as an idiom describing Elijah's body rather than his clothing; other English translations render the same Hebrew phrase as a garment. The label is strong rather than explicit because Matthew's own text in this passage never names Elijah or cites 2 Kings -- that identification is made only later in this Gospel, in its own words, at 11:14 and 17:12-13.
